introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) specified in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 00/0595/3/Grp 1, Grp 2, Grp 3 and Grp 4). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (documents, workbooks and pictures supplied in the candidate folder) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP THREE - TASK I (20 marks)**

Figure 1 shows a story typed and enclosed in a frame. Your task is to type, edit and format the text as requested.

> **Dealing with COVID-19 in Cameroon**
>
> In Cameroon, there was initially a sense of optimism that, somehow, Africa, unlike other regions, would manage to avoid the catastrophic consequences of the pandemic. There was little awareness that Cameroon was most likely just a matter of a few weeks behind.
>
> By May 2020, Cameroon was the most affected country in the region and second in sub-Saharan Africa, with a quickly rising rate of infections. The scarcity of test kits obviously hides the real number of infections. Counting individual infections, recoveries and fatalities did not provide the real picture. UNAIDS advocated for a modelling of the epidemic in order to enable quantification of health-care needs and procurement.
>
> As the first COVID-19 cases were detected in Yaoundé, a small number of health-sector officials gathered with the Minister of Health to discuss and plan epidemic containment and impact mitigation measures. One of the United Nations officials was requested to be part of the group, given UNAIDS' experience in epidemic management. She underscored the need to build on existing systems and make use of the community-driven efforts of the national AIDS response. She equally advocated for frontloading investments in communication and community mobilization to prevent COVID-19 infections, using a multisectoral approach.

Source: https://www.unaids.org/en/resources/presscentre/featurestories/2020/may/20200511_covid19-cameroon

*Figure 1*

questions.enonce_markdown: State the name and version of the word processor that is installed on your computer  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The answer is read on the computer itself. Open the word processor, then *File* > *Account* (or *Help* > *About*): the window shows the product name and its version. A correct answer has the **two** parts, for example *Microsoft Word 2016* or *LibreOffice Writer 7.x*, whatever is really installed on the machine used.

*Marking idea (1 mark):* name and version both given.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch the word processor and type the text in Figure 1. Do include bounding box  *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open the word processor (a new blank document) and type the **title** **Dealing with COVID-19 in Cameroon** and the **three paragraphs** exactly as printed. Press *Enter* only at the end of the title and of each paragraph, never at the end of a line, and respect the capital letters, the numbers (COVID-19, May 2020), the accent of Yaoundé and the punctuation.

The **bounding box** is the frame around the story. Select the title and the three paragraphs and use *Home* > **Borders** > **Outside Borders** (or *Borders and Shading* > *Box*), so that one rectangle encloses all of the text, as in Figure 1. The line *Source: ...* and the caption *Figure 1* stay outside the frame.

*Marking idea (6 marks):* title (1); paragraph 1 (1); paragraph 2 (1); paragraph 3 (1); frame around the text (1); text free of typing errors (1) - indicative split.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Format the document as directed below:

- Title: Bold, center, font size: 18  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the title and apply **Bold** (Ctrl+B), **Center** (Ctrl+E) and *Font Size* **18**.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* bold and centred (1); size 18 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: - Body: Apply full (i.e., left-right) justification  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the three paragraphs of the body and click **Justify** (Ctrl+J): the text is aligned on both the left and the right edges.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* body selected (1); justify applied (1).

With the body still selected choose **12** in the *Font Size* box.

*Marking idea (1 mark):* body at 12 points.

questions.enonce_markdown: - Apply Drop Caps of two lines to the first letter of the first paragraph.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click in the first paragraph (*In Cameroon, there was initially...*), then *Insert* > **Drop Cap** > *Drop Cap Options*: **Position: Dropped**, **Lines to drop: 2**, *OK*. The letter **I** becomes a large capital over two lines. Only the first paragraph gets a drop cap.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* drop cap on the first letter of the first paragraph (1); two lines (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert a page number as a footer, positioned at the bottom left of the page.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Insert* > **Page Number** > **Bottom of Page** > choose the *Plain Number 1* style (left aligned). The page number is placed in the footer, at the left margin. If the number was inserted in another position, click in the footer and press **Align Left** (Ctrl+L).

*Marking idea (2 marks):* page number inserted in the footer (1); positioned at the bottom left (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Change the text from block paragraphing to indented paragraphing.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **block** paragraphing every paragraph starts at the left margin; in **indented** paragraphing the first line of every paragraph is pushed to the right. Select the three paragraphs, open *Home* > *Paragraph*, and in *Indentation* > *Special* choose **First line** with a value of about **1.27 cm** (0.5 inch), then *OK*. (The Tab key at the start of each paragraph also works, but the paragraph setting is cleaner.)

*Marking idea (2 marks):* paragraphs selected (1); first-line indent applied to every paragraph (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Search for all occurrences of COVID-19 and change the text colour to red and background colour to yellow.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use **Find and Replace** (*Home* > *Replace*, or Ctrl+H). In *Find what* type **COVID-19**; in *Replace with* type **COVID-19** again, click *More* > *Format* and set the font colour to **Red** and the highlight (background) to **Yellow**; then click **Replace All**. Every occurrence of COVID-19 (in the title and in the paragraphs) is now red on a yellow background. (A second way is to select each occurrence with *Find* and apply the colours by hand, but it is slower and easy to forget one.)

*Marking idea (2 marks):* all the occurrences found (1); red text on yellow background (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your work as Task 1 and print a copy.
questions.corrige_markdown: Use *File* > **Save As** (or *Save*) to save the document as **Task 1** in the working folder, then *File* > **Print** (Ctrl+P): check the preview, choose the printer and click *Print*, and insert the printed copy in the booklet. No mark is printed for this step.
